questions.prompt: In the OpenAI Agents SDK, is the run context object sent to the LLM?

options.text: Yes, the model reads it at the start of every turn.
options.explanation: The docs say it is not sent to the LLM. Only your code and tools can read it.

options.text: Only when an agent is called as a tool by another agent.
options.explanation: Nested runs share the app state, but the docs do not send it to the model in that case either.

options.text: No, it is a local object that tools and callbacks read.
options.explanation: Right. Put model-visible facts in the input or a tool result instead.

questions.prompt: Why does Anthropic's lead research agent save its plan to Memory?

options.text: To let workers read the plan, because they share its context window.
options.explanation: Workers do not share the lead's window. Each subagent has its own.

options.text: The context can be truncated above 200,000 tokens; the plan must stay.
options.explanation: Right. Saving the plan outside the window lets the lead keep it after a cut.

options.text: To make the final answer shorter before it is passed to the citation step.
options.explanation: The plan is saved to survive truncation. It does not shorten the answer.

questions.prompt: Two Claude Code agent teammates try to claim the same task at the same moment. What stops a clash?

options.text: Task claiming uses file locking, so only one teammate gets the task.
options.explanation: Right. The docs say claiming uses file locking to prevent race conditions.

options.text: The lead approves each claim before the teammate starts.
options.explanation: The lead does not referee claims. Claiming is handled by file locking in the shared task list.

options.text: Each teammate keeps a private copy of the list, and the copies are merged later.
options.explanation: Teammates share one task list. They do not merge private copies.
